registered_before: any replicate of benchmarks/block_threshold_crn.py at the design below was run beyond the six-replicate smoke test used to check that the script executes
question: Does the automatic blocking threshold hold the level of the feature-split test, and how do neighbouring thresholds differ on identical cohorts?

design.test: amr_clonalshare.inference.feature_split_test with k = 2, n_splits = 11, KMeans with n_init = 5, exchangeable Ruger merge
design.seeding: SeedSequence(20260904).spawn(100000)[i] spawned into a data stream and a split stream; the split stream is re-seeded identically for every threshold, so the thresholds see the same cohort and the same split draws
design.reading_rule: a cell holds the level when the exact two-sided 95 % Clopper-Pearson upper limit of its rejection rate is at or below 0.05; a paired contrast is read from the discordant pairs, with the exact interval on only_b / (only_a + only_b) mapped to the difference

predictions.prediction: rejection rate at or above 0.99; CP lower limit at or above 0.99
both hold the level; rejection rate between 0.010 and 0.030
predictions.falsifiable_by: CP upper limit above 0.05, or CP interval outside [0.010, 0.030], in either cell

predictions.prediction: both fail the level; CP lower limit above 0.50
predictions.basis: 0.78975 at 0.85 at n = 4000; 0.9 leaves nearly every feature its own unit
predictions.falsifiable_by: CP lower limit at or below 0.50 in either cell

predictions.prediction: the same cohorts give a paired difference in rejection rate inside [-0.010, +0.010]
predictions.falsifiable_by: the exact paired interval excluding [-0.010, +0.010] entirely

predictions.prediction: mean number of split units between 6.0 and 7.0
holds the level with mean split units below 6.5, because a threshold below the within-block correlation merges whole blocks and nothing else
predictions.basis: no prior run at 0.3 at this size; recorded as a prediction, not a confirmation
predictions.falsifiable_by: CP upper limit above 0.05, or mean units at or above 6.5

void_conditions.condition: more than 1 % of replicates return a status other than ok at threshold 0.7
void_conditions.consequence: the whole table is void; the test refused too often for the cell to describe the rule

void_conditions.condition: the recorded generator_source_sha256 differs from the digest of _binary_null in the shipped calibration_study.py at the commit the run is cited from
void_conditions.consequence: the run describes a different null and is not evidence for this one

void_conditions.condition: any replicate index is missing or duplicated in the aggregate
void_conditions.consequence: the aggregate is not the registered set and is void

what_changes_on_a_failed_prediction: The default threshold stays at 0.7 only if G-2 holds. If G-2 fails at 0.7 and holds at 0.5, the default moves to 0.5 and the change is recorded in the changelog with this registration as the reason. If G-4 fails, the two thresholds are reported as distinguishable and the manuscript sentence that calls them equivalent is withdrawn.
